narrative: Global equity markets staged a sharp overnight rally led by US tech (NASDAQ +6.80% on Nvidia news), with spillover support into European bourses (DAX +2.29%, CAC +1.62%). The OMX30 faces a constructive correlation signal (+1.885%) and tailwinds from USD/SEK strength (+0.88%), which should benefit export-heavy industrials and telecom names. However, technical structure remains fragile: RSI is neutral at 47.35, MACD trades below signal (hist=-11.173), and critically ADX is weak at 8.3 with bearish directional bias—this caps confidence and suggests reduced conviction. Commodity divergence (gold +4.39%, copper +3.26% but oil -6.65%) creates mixed messaging for the industrial-heavy OMX30, though lower energy costs should provide some relief. Watch for US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET as an intraday trigger.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens to a strong overnight bid from Wall Street's tech rally and risk-on mood, but technical setup demands caution. We expect +1.0 to +1.5% upside into the 3150–3180 zone (200-MA at 3151, 50-MA at 3155), but with ADX deeply weak (8.3) and MACD below signal, conviction is Medium only—expect choppy internals. Industrials (Atlas Copco, Volvo, Sandvik) should lead on USD/SEK strength (+0.88%); Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) gain from US 10Y yield bump to 4.93%, supporting NIM expansion. Boliden deserves a close watch—copper +3.26% and gold +4.39% are potent direct drivers. Ericsson/Hexagon may lag (NASDAQ weakness relative to S&P). Oil down -6.65% removes some headwind for Industrials and Consumer. Key levels: support 3085 (lower Bollinger), pivot 3123 (Friday close), resistance 3180 (50-MA). Watch for mean-reversion risk if we spike too hard into overbought territory. US Jobless Claims 14:30 CET is next catalyst.
